A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenBO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original optimization experiments on ALOHA, Ehrlich functions and FoldX protein tasks, including performance, diversity, runtime and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Section 6 and Appendix C. Results retained from v2 still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The GenBO sampling-and-fitting loop, preference and robust-preference losses, forward and balanced-forward KL objectives, and proposal architectures are retained. Algorithm relocation, corrected iteration indices and renaming the raw-outcome utility from SR to Mean do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ALOHA string optimization, Ehrlich sequences of lengths 15, 32 and 64, and FoldX stability and SASA optimization of mRouge. The appendices add no dataset, domain or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within matched experiments: ALOHA retains CbAS, VSD and random mutation; Ehrlich retains CbAS, VSD, LaMBO-2 and GA; FoldX retains CbAS, VSD, LaMBO-2 and random mutation. The plotted comparator variants are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported regularization coefficient changes from λ_n = λ_0 log²(n)/n in v2 Appendix D.3 to λ_n = λ_0 log²(n) in v3 Appendix C.3. This substantively revises one stated experimental setting; unchanged result tables do not establish that experiments were rerun. Batch budgets, initial sample sizes and architecture configurations are retained.

E4.justification: The threshold-annealing sweep, Ehrlich-32 batch-size ablation and FoldX diversity analyses remain the same in Figures 5, 6 and 3, respectively. Additional prose does not introduce new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state five random seeds and shading of ±1 standard deviation. Figure 6 error bars, tabulated uncertainty and runtime standard-deviation reporting retain the same practices.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 4–6 and all empirical plots are unchanged. Appendix C.5 newly states that larger batches yield higher variability across candidates, adding a qualitative assertion about the retained Figure 6 without introducing a new measurement.

T1.justification: v3 replaces v2’s misspecification-gap theorem and realizable-case corollary with a normalization-based Theorem 1 and Lemma 5. It introduces bounded-weight and dense-model-class assumptions, revises regularization and noise assumptions, and adds a finite-domain convergence rate. Appendix B.5 also supplies new forward-KL and Bregman-divergence derivations previously only promised in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the theoretical claim from asymptotic concentration at global optima to approximation of an optimal target, and describes experiments as performance evaluation rather than demonstration of that concentration. The central surrogate-free GenBO contribution and competitive-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds a generalized Bayesian interpretation: inference over optimizer location with acquisition values serving as a pseudo-likelihood. Section 4 and Appendix B further qualify the existing target-versus-optimizer distinction by explicitly leaving regret-rate control, including sublinear cumulative regret, to future work.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C adds an experiment-code availability statement and repository address absent from v2. The documented regularization schedule is also revised. Architecture tables, threshold schedules and most other implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ament et al. (2023), Knoblauch et al. (2022), Schölkopf and Smola (2002), and Srinivas et al. (2010), supporting soft-EI, generalized-Bayesian and theoretical discussion. Boucheron et al. (2013) and Pisier (2016) are removed. Section 5’s principal comparisons with earlier optimization approaches remain.

P1.justification: The theoretical appendix is extensively reorganized into definitions, auxiliary results, assumptions, main results and loss derivations. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, and Sections 3–4 receive substantial explanatory and notation edits. This restructuring goes beyond simply appending new scientific content.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from its appendix into Section 3, existing appendix figures and tables are repositioned, Table 3 drops the SR acronym row, and several captions are refined. The empirical plots themselves and numerical-table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, code-access information and calibration of the abstract’s convergence claim. However, its replacement proof applies Lemma 1 to the normalized estimator in Equation 64 although the lemma bounds distance from the unconstrained minimizer. The new balanced-KL derivation also gives a correction-term sign in Equation 79 inconsistent with retained Equation 21. These unresolved issues in the central theoretical rewrite prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the clearer presentation and disclosure.
